fixes: before-mock-test-strategy body: replaced the external link https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in/ (not an allowed route) with 'the official GATE 2027 website (listed on the [sources page](/sources))'; /sources lists that URL in its source registry (source id gate2027-website).

roadmap final-revision links: replaced the external 'Official GATE 2027 website' link (https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in/) with {label: 'Sources (official GATE 2027 website)', href: '/sources'}; the matching activity now says the website is linked on the Sources page.

roadmap mixed-practice activities: 'Take the Foundation and Beginner → Intermediate mocks as short mixed papers' was inaccurate because content/mocks/blueprint.json makes mocks 1–7 single-subject. It now names the mixed Foundation mocks (8–10) and mocks 11–20, says that mocks 1–7 each cover one subject, and notes that none of mocks 1–20 contains General Aptitude, so GA practice should continue alongside them.

before-mock-test-strategy tier table: Foundation row now says mocks 8–10 mix the DA subjects, and the Beginner → Intermediate row no longer calls mocks 11–20 the 'first mixed papers' (8–10 are already mixed, per blueprint.json).

before-mock-test-strategy 'When to start' table: replaced the unsupported 'Often suits: Many students' with a description of who the mixed approach fits ('Students who want early exam habits without delaying the syllabus').

before-pyq-strategy: removed 'The DA paper is young.' because no source in pattern.json or papers.json supports a claim about the paper's history. The summary now says 'The official DA papers on this platform are few' instead of the unsourced 'Official DA papers are few'.

before-pyq-strategy: 'A routine that works for many students' -> 'One routine' (unsupported population claim); 'keep one paper (often the most recent)' -> '(for example, the most recent)'; 'topic-wise use usually teaches more' -> 'topic-wise use gives feedback while you are still learning'.

during-question-selection: replaced the unsupported 'few students solve everything. What separates scores is often…' with an arithmetic framing: 65 questions in 180 minutes is about 2.8 minutes per question (180/65 = 2.769), so you may not reach a confident answer on every question.

during-question-selection: 'Answer a category C MCQ only if you can genuinely eliminate at least one option' contradicted the MCQ article, which treats blind guessing (EV = 0) as a personal choice. It now says that answering has positive expected value only after a genuine elimination, that a blind guess has zero expected value, and that you should decide before the exam whether to answer those.

before-error-log: 'Most students do not lose marks at random' (unsupported population claim) -> 'Lost marks are often not random…'; 'They are the most dangerous errors, because you will not think to recheck them' -> 'They are easy to miss, because in the exam you are unlikely to recheck an answer you feel sure of.'

before-formula-revision: removed the invented quantitative claim 'Five minutes of this does more than twenty minutes of reading', replacing it with a qualitative statement that recall tests whether you can produce the formula; 'Most formula mistakes in an exam are not about forgetting a formula entirely' (unsupported) -> 'Forgetting a formula entirely is only one way to get it wrong. Another is misapplying a condition'; 'A common middle path' -> 'One middle path'.

before-revision-strategy: 'Many students combine daily small doses…' -> 'The rhythms can also be combined…'; 'A common structure is' -> 'One structure is'; 'one of the fastest revisions available' (unsupported superlative) -> 'a quick, targeted revision'.

time-order-of-attack: summary 'Four commonly used orders' -> 'Four orders' (usage frequency unsupported); 'Many students settle on a mixture' -> 'The orders can also be mixed'; 'Some questions span two subjects' (the platform tags each PYQ with exactly one subject) -> 'A question can also draw on more than one subject (a probability calculation inside a machine learning question, say)'.
time-two-pass-vs-three-pass: 'Often suits: most students as a starting point' (unsupported population claim) -> 'anyone without a settled approach yet, as a starting point'.
during-rough-work: 'Many calculation errors are misread handwriting' -> 'Some calculation errors come from misread handwriting'.

during-calculation-traps-and-calculator: 'Calculation errors are rarely fixed by "being more careful"' (unsupported frequency claim) -> 'Resolving to "be more careful" gives you nothing specific to do. Specific checks that you run every time do.'

before-syllabus-completion: made the least-squares statement precise. The normal equations X^T X beta-hat = X^T y are not themselves 'a projection onto the column space'; the fitted vector X beta-hat is the orthogonal projection of y onto col(X). Also 'Two common ways' -> 'Two ways'.
method: Independent review of content/strategy/articles.json (16 articles) and content/roadmap.json (10 stages). Exam facts were checked against content/exam/pattern.json and content/exam/papers.json: 65 questions, 100 marks, 180 minutes; GA Q.1–5 at 1 mark and Q.6–10 at 2 marks; DA Q.11–35 at 1 mark and Q.36–65 at 2 marks; MCQ −1/3 and −2/3; no negative marks for MSQ or NAT; no MSQ partial credit; NAT answer ranges; virtual calculator; 2026 session times. The data were cross-checked against all 195 PYQ files: per-question marks match in every paper, each paper totals 100, and the DA section interleaves subjects in all three papers (36–42 subject runs per paper), which supports the order-of-attack claim. python3 recomputed every number: 1.8 min/mark, 180/65≈2.77 min/question, 0.56 marks/min, the proportional budgets (27/45/108 and 24/40/96+20), the default and DA-first checkpoint splits, the pass splits (125+45+10, 70+85+25), the rereading cost (12.5 and 18.75 min), the MCQ expected values with exact fractions (0, 1/9, 1/3; doubled for 2 marks; break-even p=1/4), 2^4−1=15 MSQ selections, 1.41²×50=99.405, and the Python operator results. Platform claims were verified against the source: mock tiers and lengths (content/mocks/tests.json, blueprint.json), the timer's default checkpoints (timer-logic.ts), mastery levels and the 3-attempt minimum (analytics/stats.ts), the seven mistake types, error-log auto-logging, the Practice quick sets, the palette states and the scoring of answered-and-marked questions. A phrase scan flagged universal or population claims (most/many/few students, superlatives, invented ratios) for rewriting. All 16 multi-approach topics present at least two options with gains and costs (subject order, PYQ sequencing, revision rhythms, mock timing, memorise vs derive, first-pass styles, order of attack, number of passes, GA scheduling); no GATE statistics, cut-offs, rank predictions, topper claims or 'always appears' claims were found. Internal links: every href resolves to an allowed route or to /strategy/<id> for an existing, non-reserved article id (the dynamic route src/app/(app)/strategy/[id], which is also the URL search uses); the 2 external links were replaced with /sources. All 102 KaTeX segments render. validate-file.ts reports only the path-level 'no per-file validator' warning, and build.ts --validate-only shows 0 warnings and no errors for strategy or roadmap (its 24 errors are unrelated missing mock questions, mock-26 to mock-50).
